name: add_criterion
description:
Adds a new acceptance criterion to a story.

Use get_story to see existing criteria before adding.

name: analyze_story_linkage
description:
Analyze story-component linkage in the project.

Returns a report showing unlinked stories, broken links, linked stories
grouped by component, and orphan components with no stories.

name: assign_epic_to_working_copy
description:
Say which checkout an epic is built on.

Its own action, deliberately. John: *"I think for the time being we should
keep this flexible so let's have these as separate actions — creating the
working copy and assigning an epic to a working copy."*

So approving an epic is agreement, and this is placement, and neither implies
the other. That leaves room for the decision to be made by whoever is best
placed to make it: *"if there's an appropriate working copy and agent then it
should get assigned that, or maybe the agent wants a fresh working copy ...
the user should be able to decide where to assign it or the agent should be
able to decide."*

Call `list_working_copies` first. A copy with no `root` has no disk behind it
and is refused here rather than accepted and discovered later — that failure
already has an issue of its own (28e838cc), where an epic reported it was
being built on a directory that did not exist.

## What it writes

The epic's **stories**, not the epic. An epic has no place in the requirement
graph — nothing in `RequirementCalculator` or `Predicates` mentions one — so a
copy recorded on the epic was never consulted when deciding what an agent is
offered. The column named a routing nothing performed, and an agent told to
release an epic looked for the step that would do it and found none.

The binding lives on `stories.working_copy_id`, which is the grain
`get_next_requirement` actually reads. John: *"an epic is just basically a
convenience measure to act on multiple stories ... these assignments need to
go into the story because that's how the graph works."*

So this stays one call and one act, and it now has an effect: the epic's
stories go to that checkout, its agents are offered them, and no other copy
is.

## What this does not do

It does not start an agent. Assigning and starting are separate for the same
reason approving and assigning are: an epic can sit on a checkout that already
has an agent working, and giving it one of its own would be a second agent
nobody asked for.

epic_id.description: Id of the epic to place

working_copy_id.description: Id of the checkout to build it on, from list_working_copies

name: assign_story_to_epic
description:
Moves a story into an epic.

A story belongs to at most one epic, so this is a move rather than an add —
the story leaves whatever epic it was in. Omit `epic_name` to remove the
story from its epic entirely.

Assignment does not change readiness.

epic_name.description: Destination epic name. Omit to remove the story from its epic.

name: assign_story_to_working_copy
description: Add a story on a working copy's queue.

working_copy_id.description: Working copy whose queue to edit

name: clear_story_component
description:
Removes the component link from a story.

Use this when a story is no longer satisfied by its assigned component.

name: create_epic
description:
Creates an epic — a named collection of user stories.

Epics are **organizational only**. Putting a story in an epic does not
release it for development; that is `ready_for_dev` on the story itself.
Use `set_epic_stories_ready` to release a whole epic in one go.

name: create_story
description:
Creates a user story.

The story sentence and the agent's working notes are separate fields:
`story` holds "As a [role], I want [goal] so that [value]" and nothing
else; `notes` is where mechanism, dependencies and caveats go.

New stories are **not ready for development** — they produce no
requirements until released. Use `update_story` with
`ready_for_dev: true`, or release a whole epic at once.

Acceptance criteria are NOT created here — they emerge from Three
Amigos as rule-bearing scenarios, never invented up-front. Run
`start_three_amigos_session` after creating the story.

Example:
  title: "User Login"
  story: "As a user, I want to log in so I can access my account"
  notes: "Blocked on the identity provider migration"

description.description: Legacy alias for `story`. Prefer `story`; the two are kept in sync.

notes.description: Working notes for the agent — mechanism, dependencies, caveats (optional)

priority.description: Priority order (1 = highest). Lower numbers are higher priority.

story.description: User story in 'As a [role], I want [goal] so that [value]' format. The role MUST be a real human (user, admin, manager) - never a system, API, or service. Keep it to the sentence — mechanism, dependencies and caveats belong in `notes`. Either `story` or `description` must be given; they are kept in sync.

name: get_criterion
description:
Reads one acceptance criterion by its number, retired or active.

Retired criteria are not listed by `get_story`; this is how to read one.

name: get_story
description:
Gets a single story by number with full details including acceptance criteria.

Use list_story_titles to find story numbers if you don't know them.

name: link_criterion_to_rule
description:
Links an existing acceptance criterion to a Three Amigos rule.

Updates `Criterion.rule_id` only — the criterion's description, kind,
body, and verification status are untouched. Use after `add_criterion`
to associate the new criterion with the rule it belongs under (the
`add_criterion` tool itself only creates the criterion at story level
and leaves `rule_id` nil).

Cannot relink verified (locked) criteria. Returns an error if the
rule_id does not reference an existing rule on this project.

rule_id.description: Rule UUID to attach the criterion to (from list_rules)

name: list_epics
description:
Lists the active project's epics with their story counts and how many of
each epic's stories are released for development.

This is a backlog tool — it reaches stories the development graph hides.

name: list_project_tags
description:
Lists all tags used in the project.

Shows all available tags that have been applied to stories or components.
Use this to see what organizational categories exist.

name: list_stories
description:
Lists stories in a project with pagination.

Returns full story details including criteria. For a lightweight
list of just titles, use list_story_titles instead.

epic.description: Filter to one epic, by slug or id as printed by list_epics — the stories that epic contains (optional)

project_id.description: Must match this connection's own project, or the call is refused — a session's tools cannot read a different project's stories (79873d5a)

ready_for_dev.description: Filter by readiness. Pass false to see the parked backlog — the stories the development graph hides (optional)

without_epic.description: Pass true to see only stories not yet assigned to any epic — useful when grouping stories into epics (optional)

name: list_story_titles
description:
Lists story titles in a project (lightweight).

Returns just number, title, and component_id - no criteria or full descriptions.
Use this for quick lookups, selection lists, or when you need to find a story number.

From a script this answers with records rather than the listing, so the
titles can be filtered and counted without parsing prose.

name: move_criterion
description:
Moves an acceptance criterion from its current story to a different story.

Cannot move verified (locked) criteria - they are protected from changes.
Any existing rule link is cleared during the move, since BDD rules are
story-scoped and would otherwise point across story boundaries.
Use get_story to see criterion numbers and their verification status.

target_story_number.description: Number of the story to move the criterion to

name: propose_epic
description:
Send an epic to the user for approval.

The main agent's half of the hand-off, and the only way work on an epic ever
starts. Approving it is the user's act, on the epics screen — John: *"the
agent sending it and the meatbags approving it are two different things."*
This tool does the sending and nothing else: no working copy is chosen, no
agent is started, nothing is spent.

## When to call it

When the `work_dispatched` requirement is unsatisfied. That happens only when
nothing is being built *and* there are ready stories nobody has been given —
the one state that wants you to act. If something is already underway, leave
it alone; an agent working on a story is a reason not to assign more.

Group the ready stories into an epic with `create_epic` and
`assign_story_to_epic` first, then propose it.

## What the user sees

The epic appears on their epics screen with a control to agree to it, and the
screen updates while they are looking at it. Until they agree, nothing
happens — an epic they ignore changes nothing.

epic_id.description: Id of the epic to send for approval

name: release_story_from_working_copy
description:
Free a story from whatever working copy holds it, with nowhere new to go
yet -- the explicit reassign path `set_active_story` names when a story is
held elsewhere (3f824f74): free it here, then select it on the copy that
should take it.

Main agent only, the same restriction `set_active_story` places on naming
another copy's `working_copy_id` -- this reaches across copies the same
way.

force.description: Free it even though the copy holding it has it as its team's active story. Without this, that refuses -- the team there may be mid-work on it.

name: restore_criterion
description:
Brings a retired acceptance criterion back, under the same number.

A spec file that names the number covers it again.

name: restore_story
description:
Brings a retired story back under its number, with the criteria that were
retired with it.

The story comes back parked. Release it with
`update_story(ready_for_dev: true)` to put it back to work.

name: retire_criterion
description:
Retires an acceptance criterion. There is no delete.

A retired criterion keeps its number, which is never given to another, and
drops out of its story's coverage. `restore_criterion` brings it back.
No file is deleted: the result lists every spex on your working copy that
now covers nothing (its own, and any other naming a number that is not a
live criterion). Delete those in your copy and commit.

name: retire_story
description:
Retires a user story. There is no delete.

A retired story keeps its number, which is never given to another story,
leaves the backlog and the graph, and its criteria retire with it. Linked
issues keep their link.

name: set_active_story
description:
Select the story the team on the current working copy works on.

Whoever calls it — a team member, the main agent, a session — the story goes
to the whole team, the copy's coding and QA agents, who see it through
together (a31f1cd6, `Agents.assign_team/3`).

The main agent steers a feature copy's team by naming it with
`working_copy_id`; anyone else selects for their own copy only. The main copy
itself is never given a story: work is promoted to it, not done on it.

story_number.description: Number of the story for this copy's team to work on. It must be ready for development and not assigned to another copy. Every coding and QA agent on the copy takes it; the story they held before is released. Omit to clear it.

working_copy_id.description: Id of the feature copy whose team takes the story, from list_working_copies. Only the main agent may name another copy; everyone else selects for their own.

name: set_epic_stories_ready
description:
Releases (or parks) every story currently in an epic, in one shot.

This is a **bulk edit of the stories**, not a property of the epic. Stories
added to the epic afterwards are unaffected and stay parked — the epic
carries no readiness of its own and nothing cascades later.

ready_for_dev.description: true to release the epic's stories for development, false to park them

name: set_story_component
description: Links a story to the component that implements it, by module name.

name: start_story_interview
description:
Starts a guided story interview with the PM — develop and refine bare
user stories through structured questioning. Acceptance criteria are
out of scope; those land later in a Three Amigos session
(see `start_three_amigos_session`).

Delegates prompt building to `CodeMySpec.AgentTasks.StoryInterview`.

name: start_story_review
description:
Starts a story-level review with the PM — evaluate completeness and
quality of existing bare user stories. Acceptance criteria are not
reviewed here; those are produced and reviewed during Three Amigos.

Delegates prompt building to `CodeMySpec.AgentTasks.StoryInterview`.

name: start_three_amigos_session
description:
Starts a Three Amigos / Example Mapping session on a single story.

Returns the protocol prompt the agent uses to drive the workshop with
the PM — persona linkage, rules (blue cards), scenarios (green cards),
and questions (red cards). Delegates prompt building to
`CodeMySpec.AgentTasks.ThreeAmigos`.

name: tag_stories
description:
Adds a tag to multiple stories at once.

Useful for bulk categorization when organizing stories by domain.

## Tag naming

Tags can be simple (`notifications`, `urgent`) or use colon syntax for
typed/namespaced tags (`epic:verification-flow`, `persona:driver`).

The colon syntax is useful for organizing stories into categories that
can be filtered, e.g., `list_stories(tag: "persona:driver")`.

tag.description: Tag name to apply to all stories

name: triage_issues
description:
Starts a triage session for incoming external issues.

Fetches incoming issues and story titles, then returns a structured
prompt guiding through triage decisions:
- Obvious bug → accept the issue
- Requires story change → update/create story, accept with story_number
- Not valid → dismiss with reason

min_severity.description: Minimum severity to triage: critical, high, medium (default), low, info

name: unassign_epic_from_working_copy
description: Remove a epic on a working copy's queue.

working_copy_id.description: Working copy whose queue to edit

name: unassign_story_from_working_copy
description: Remove a story on a working copy's queue.

working_copy_id.description: Working copy whose queue to edit

name: update_epic
description:
Renames an epic or rewrites what it says it covers.

An epic's description is where the decisions that hold across its stories
live — the shared rules, the things each story has to answer. That is exactly
the text that goes stale first, because deciding to drop a story is a decision
*about* the epic, and until now the only way to correct it was to build a
second epic beside the first and move everything into it.

Renaming keeps the slug the epic already had. A slug that moves breaks every
link anybody saved to it, and a name is a label rather than an identity.

name: update_story
description:
Updates a user story.

A story's criteria are not touched here. They change only through the
criterion tools (`add_criterion`, `retire_criterion`), so each keeps
its number for life.

## Tags

Tags can be simple (`urgent`) or namespaced (`epic:auth`, `persona:admin`).
Use `list_stories(tag: "...")` to filter by tag.

description.description: New description in 'As a [role], I want [goal] so that [value]' format. Role must be a real human, not a system or technical component (optional)

epic_id.description: Move the story into this epic, or pass null to take it out. Prefer `assign_story_to_epic`, which takes the epic's name (optional)

priority.description: Priority order (1 = highest). Lower numbers are higher priority. (optional)

ready_for_dev.description: Release the story for development, or park it. Parked stories produce no requirements in the development graph (optional)

story.description: User-story sentence in 'As a [role], I want [goal] so that [value]' format. Keep it to the sentence — mechanism and caveats belong in `notes` (optional)
